clue.text: Tom Cruise: point out films

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of the actor's name and the following word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A director tells Tom Cruise to point at the camera, as though giving stage directions about films.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the fourteen letters of TOM CRUISE and POINT.
explanation.definitionFit: Motion pictures is the older formal term for movies, so it is a plain synonym for films.

clue.text: Hello! celebrity that might have shoot in bed?

definitions.text: that might have shoot in bed?
definitions.note: a description standing for a noun: a climbing plant that sends up shoots in a flower bed (with a cheeky second sense)

parts.note: Morning! is a greeting, short for Good morning
glory means fame or renown, as celebrity does

explanation.surface: Reads like a gossip-magazine headline about a celebrity photo shoot in bed, with Hello! the magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: Hello! looks like the celebrity magazine, but it is just a greeting. The definition also winks at the British slang sense of a man's morning arousal.
explanation.definitionFit: The climbing flower of that name grows in garden beds and sends out shoots, so it is a thing that might have shoot in a bed.

clue.text: Fans sent to cup round matches

indicators.note: to cup is to hold within the hands, so the shuffled letters wrap round the next piece
to fan is to spread out, so the letters of the word sent are spread into a new order

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: Football supporters are sent off to watch cup ties in a round of matches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fans' rearranges SENT to TNES, which 'to cup' wraps round O.
explanation.definitionFit: A colour that tones with another harmonises with it, so it goes with or matches it.

clue.text: Forgets about beauty

parts.note: over can mean about or concerning, as in fussing over something
good looks means beauty

explanation.surface: Someone forgets all about beauty, as if neglecting their appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: To fail to notice or to ignore something is to forget it, so the verbs are close synonyms.

clue.text: Norm to steal plant

parts.note: par is the standard or norm, as in below par
to snip, like to nip, is informal for to pinch or snatch something

explanation.surface: It is normal practice to steal a plant, as gardeners pinching cuttings might say.
explanation.definitionFit: The parsnip is a root vegetable, so it is an example of a plant.

clue.text: TV detective to search old house for clue, essentially

indicators.note: to house is to contain, so the first pair of pieces holds the middle letters inside

parts.note: to comb an area is to search it thoroughly

indicators.note: essentially means at its core, so take the middle letters of the word clue

explanation.surface: A TV detective goes to search an old house for the key clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' looks like a noun but is a verb meaning hold inside; 'essentially' takes the heart of the word clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieutenant Columbo, played by Peter Falk, is the famously scruffy television sleuth, so the name is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Top McDonald's? One does egg

indicators.note: to top something is to cut off its head, so the first letter is removed

parts.note: a burger is what McDonald's sells

explanation.surface: Asks what is top at McDonald's, then mentions egg, as if discussing the menu's breakfast options.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' is a verb here: behead BURGER. 'egg' is the verb, as in egg someone on.
explanation.definitionFit: To egg someone on is to urge them, so one who does that is a person who urges.

clue.text: Old lover in? See TV set that's wide

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: set can mean arranged or put in order, so these letters are placed in a new order

explanation.surface: An ex asks to come in to watch the television set, wide-screen perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' looks like the TV set but rearranges IN and SEE TV to TENSIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extensive covers a large area or range, so it is broad or wide.

clue.text: Wash up around noon

indicators.note: around means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: to rise is to get up

explanation.surface: Someone washes up the dishes at about midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wash up' looks like a phrase; 'Wash' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To rinse is to clean with water, a light form of washing, so it is a synonym.

clue.text: Agree let for building and move to a worse place

indicators.note: building means constructing something new from the materials, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Planners agree to let land for building, and a team is moved down a division.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' rearranges AGREE LET.
explanation.definitionFit: A team that is relegated drops to a lower division, so it is moved to a worse place.

clue.text: Place for swingers? Taking the car key in the middle, getting kinky gran

parts.note: driving is taking the car out on the road

indicators.note: kinky means twisted, so the letters of the word gran are twisted into a new order
in the middle means take the central letter of the word key

explanation.surface: A racy story: a swingers' party where car keys go into a bowl and granny gets kinky.
explanation.walkthrough: The swingers are golfers, not partner-swappers; 'kinky' twists the letters of gran.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers practise their swings at a driving range, so it is literally a place for those who swing clubs.

clue.text: Drug and endless drink — one litre knocked back entering pub

indicators.note: entering means these letters go inside the word for pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: to sup is to drink

indicators.note: knocked back means turned round, so the pair of letters reads the other way

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A drinker in a pub knocks back a litre of drink, with drugs on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like drinking but turns IL into LI; 'endless' trims the drink and 'entering' sends both inside the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: This hormone is given as a medicine to diabetics, so it counts as a drug.

clue.text: Sailor in a state right to cross river

indicators.note: to cross here means to go through, so the letter for right passes into the other letters

parts.note: Maine is a US state

explanation.surface: A sailor in a state of distress has the right to cross a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cross' sends the letter for right through the state, just after its second letter, with the river's R at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A mariner is a seaman, the literary word for one who sails, so it is a synonym for sailor.

clue.text: Scales on this being electronic, (approximately) 0kg returned to screen

indicators.note: to screen is to shield or hide, so the reversed letters enclose the other two
returned means sent back, so these letters read the other way

parts.note: zero is read as the letter O, then K and G from kilograms
E is the usual abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail
C stands for circa, Latin for about or approximately

explanation.surface: Electronic scales show roughly zero kilograms, as if reading a weighing machine's screen.
explanation.walkthrough: The scales are on a lizard, not a weighing machine. 'returned' turns OKG into GKO; 'to screen' puts EC inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gecko is a small lizard with a scaly skin, so it is a creature that has scales on it.

clue.text: Came to continent, when missing fine country

parts.note: to come to an amount is to cost it

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the letter for fine is dropped

parts.note: Africa is a continent
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A traveller arrives on a continent and, unpaid fine notwithstanding, enters a country.
explanation.definitionFit: The Central American republic between Nicaragua and Panama is an example of a country.

clue.text: He scored for City by cutting inside

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: cutting inside means going in among other letters, so the two letters are placed within the city

parts.note: Kiev is the Ukrainian capital city
of can mean by, as in a work of a given author

explanation.surface: A footballer scores for City by cutting inside past a defender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He scored' means composed a score, not a goal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian composer of Peter and the Wolf wrote musical scores, so he is a man who scored.

clue.text: So, bitter struggles with Conservative dealing with Labour

indicators.note: struggles suggests thrashing about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A political report: bitter struggles between the Conservatives and the Labour party.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour here is childbirth, not the political party.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstetrics is the branch of medicine concerned with childbirth, so an obstetric matter is one about labour.

clue.text: Breaking point? Carries on returning growth

parts.note: lasts means continues or carries on

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word for growth reads the other way

parts.note: a wart is a small growth on the skin

explanation.surface: Someone at breaking point carries on, though an unwanted growth keeps coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns WART into TRAW.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the final addition that makes something unbearable, the point at which patience breaks.

clue.text: Entertainer embarrassed on film

parts.note: an embarrassed person goes red
a film is a thin layer, as is a coat

explanation.surface: An entertainer is embarrassed to appear on film.
explanation.walkthrough: A redcoat is a holiday-camp entertainer at Butlin's, the British holiday-camp chain, named for the red jackets worn.
explanation.definitionFit: Staff at British holiday camps who entertain guests are known by their red jackets, so the name means an entertainer.

clue.text: Lighter Wise partly obscured by old Morecambe's feature?

indicators.note: partly obscured means some of the word is hidden from view, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: the surname of the comedian Ernie Wise, taken as written
the seaside town of Morecambe in Lancashire had piers, since demolished, hence old

explanation.surface: Ernie Wise partly hidden behind Eric Morecambe's famous glasses, the comedy double act Morecambe and Wise.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe looks like Eric Morecambe, Ernie Wise's comedy partner, but it is the seaside town, whose old pier is the feature.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wispy is thin and insubstantial, so a wispier thing is lighter or flimsier.

clue.text: Brilliance of healthcare provider in recession without drugs

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the reversed letters go round the drugs
in recession means going backwards, so these three letters read the other way

parts.note: the NHS, Britain's National Health Service, provides healthcare
E is slang for the drug ecstasy, so two of them are drugs

explanation.surface: A news item: the cash-strapped health service in a recession goes without drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in recession' gives SHN; 'without' is the old sense outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheen is a soft shine on a surface, so it is a kind of lustre or brilliance.

clue.text: Did cook in oven: raw on the outside

indicators.note: on the outside means the first word goes round the second

parts.note: red can mean raw or sore, as with red, inflamed skin, or underdone meat
an oast is a kiln for drying hops, a kind of oven

explanation.surface: Something was cooked in the oven but stayed raw on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: An oast house is a British hop-drying kiln.
explanation.definitionFit: To roast is to cook in an oven, so the past tense matches 'did cook'.

clue.text: Sound from plucking pheasant, ultimately hung up to eat

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so take the final letter of pheasant
in a down clue, hung up means raised, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to gnaw is to eat by biting

explanation.surface: A cook plucks a pheasant that has been hung up before it is eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: Plucking is of strings, not feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: A twang is the ringing note made when a string is plucked, so it is the sound from plucking.

clue.text: Is one hot in sun? Conditions not hot

parts.note: S is a standard abbreviation for sun or Sunday

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter for hot is dropped

parts.note: the weather is the conditions outside
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Asks whether someone is hot in the sun and answers that conditions are not hot.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who sweats is one who is hot, so the word also names a perspirer as well as a jumper.

clue.text: Bones of soldiers? Cause of pain?

parts.note: the TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve soldiers
RSI is repetitive strain injury, which causes pain

explanation.surface: Asks whether broken bones are why soldiers are in pain.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the small bones of the ankle and foot, so the word names a set of bones.

clue.text: Pasta cook visiting Italy to adopt cooking

parts.note: to cook or rig the books is to falsify them

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so the first letters take the next pair inside

parts.note: visiting a place is being at it
I is the international vehicle code for Italy
if something is cooking it is on, as in what's on

explanation.surface: A chef visiting Italy takes up the local cooking and makes pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cook' is the fiddling sense, and 'to adopt' puts ON inside ATI.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigatoni are ridged tubes of pasta, so the word is an example of pasta.

clue.text: Getting into period drama on TV (repeat)

indicators.note: getting into means entering, so the two letters go inside the other word

parts.note: a run is a period of time, as in a run of good luck
ER is the American hospital drama series

explanation.surface: Someone gets hooked on a period drama on TV, which turns out to be a repeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'period drama' looks like one phrase, but 'period' and 'drama on TV' are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A rerun is a television programme shown again, so it is a noun meaning a repeat.

clue.text: Get better shots with this model? Great plastic surgery

parts.note: the Model T was the famous early Ford car

indicators.note: plastic means mouldable, so the letters of great are reshaped

parts.note: a doctor's surgery is a practice, as in a GP practice

explanation.surface: A model with great plastic surgery gets better photo shots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plastic' rearranges GREAT into ARGET. 'shots' means shooting at a mark, not photographs.
explanation.definitionFit: Shooting repeatedly at a mark is how marksmen improve, so this activity helps you get better shots.
